problem_text:
A city planner needs to allocate the annual budget across 10 infrastructure projects to maximize the total projected benefit to the community. The characteristics of each project are as follows:
* Project A: projected benefit is 0.106, disruption index is 0.238, allocation bounds [0.021, 0.392]
* Project B: projected benefit is 0.052, disruption index is 0.116, allocation bounds [0.080, 0.554]
* Project C: projected benefit is 0.092, disruption index is 0.280, allocation bounds [0.083, 0.526]
* Project D: projected benefit is 0.077, disruption index is 0.068, allocation bounds [0.007, 0.569]
* Project E: projected benefit is 0.152, disruption index is 0.299, allocation bounds [0.085, 0.659]
* Project F: projected benefit is 0.134, disruption index is 0.062, allocation bounds [0.080, 0.649]
* Project G: projected benefit is 0.194, disruption index is 0.233, allocation bounds [0.067, 0.621]
* Project H: projected benefit is 0.161, disruption index is 0.018, allocation bounds [0.014, 0.854]
* Project I: projected benefit is 0.079, disruption index is 0.221, allocation bounds [0.030, 0.822]
* Project J: projected benefit is 0.070, disruption index is 0.283, allocation bounds [0.025, 0.551]
Each project must receive a budget share that satisfies its individual minimum and maximum allocation limits, and the total of all budget shares must sum to one. To ensure adequate community engagement, the planner requires that the group of outreach-focused projects, represented by the subset L = {J}, collectively receive at least 0.041 of the total budget. At the same time, the overall portfolio disruption, measured by a composite disruption index, must not exceed 0.215, and the total projected benefit of the portfolio must be no less than 0.091. Please determine the optimal budget allocation that maximizes the total projected benefit while satisfying all constraints.
